description: Bidirectional, zero-drift, PWM-rejection current-sense amplifier, A1 gain grade (20 V/V), D (SOIC-8) package.

pinout.name: IN-
pinout.notes: Analog input. Connect to load side of shunt resistor.

pinout.name: REF2
pinout.notes: Reference 2 voltage input, 0V to VS. Do not connect to a voltage source lower than GND or higher than VS.

pinout.name: NC
pinout.notes: Reserved. Connect to ground or leave floating.

pinout.name: REF1
pinout.notes: Reference 1 voltage input, 0V to VS. Do not connect to a voltage source lower than GND or higher than VS.

pinout.name: IN+
pinout.notes: Analog input. Connect to supply side of shunt resistor.

decoupling.placement: as close as possible to the supply and ground pins
decoupling.notes: Additional decoupling capacitance can be added to compensate for noisy or high-impedance power supplies (Power Supply Decoupling section).

land_pattern.notes: IPC land pattern from TI's example board layout: 8x pads 0.6mm x 1.55mm at 1.27mm pitch, non-solder-mask-defined preferred. No exposed pad on this package.

layout_notes: Input filters are not required for accurate measurement and are not recommended at the input pins; if used, keep series resistors <=10 ohm (added series R creates differential error via internal bias-current mismatch) and prefer filtering at the amplifier output instead.
Use a Kelvin (4-wire) connection from the current-sense shunt resistor to the IN+/IN- pins; poor routing adds series impedance that causes measurement error given the very low shunt resistance.
Provide adequate bypass capacitance on the VS pin, placed as close as possible to the supply/ground pins, for high-precision applications.
Recommended board layout (both TSSOP and SOIC examples) routes IN+/IN- directly to the shunt with vias to the ground plane near GND and REF2/NC, and places CBYPASS next to VS.
Do not connect REF1 or REF2 to any voltage source below GND or above VS; there is no operational difference between the two reference pins.
